title: Schematic closure of a quasi-compact open subspace
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $j:O\hookrightarrow B$ be a quasi-compact open immersion. There is a smallest closed subspace $C\hookrightarrow B$ through which $j$ factors, called its schematic closure. The map $O\to C$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, its image is topologically dense in $C$, and $\mathcal O_C\to j_*\mathcal O_O$ is injective; this last property is called schematic density. Formation of $C$ commutes with etale base change on $B$, hence with restriction to every open subspace of $B$. In particular, over an open subspace $V\subseteq B$ in which $O$ is closed, one has $C\times_BV=O\times_BV$ as closed subspaces of $V$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_B\to j_*\mathcal O_O)$. An open immersion is separated: its relative diagonal is an isomorphism, since it is an inclusion of subfunctors; an isomorphism is a closed immersion on every scheme test. Thus the quasi-compact separated direct-image theorem makes $j_*\mathcal O_O$ quasi-coherent. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent (its local presentation has one generator and no relations), so the kernel theorem makes $\mathcal I$ quasi-coherent. It is an ideal because it is the kernel of a ring map. Let $c:C=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow B$ be the closed subspace supplied by the ideal correspondence.

proof.text: The composite $\mathcal I\to j_*\mathcal O_O$ is zero, so the factorization criterion gives $q:O\to C$ with $cq=j$. If $D\hookrightarrow B$ is any closed subspace through which $j$ factors, its defining ideal $\mathcal J$ maps to zero in $j_*\mathcal O_O$. Therefore $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$. The inclusion-reversing correspondence gives $C\subseteq D$. This proves existence and minimality; two minimal closed subspaces are equal as subfunctors.

proof.text: For an etale map $g:B\prime\to B$, the direct-image restriction comparison identifies the ring map for $j\prime:O\times_BB\prime\to B\prime$ with the restriction of the ring map for $j$. Kernels are computed on sections, and restricting to the localized etale site keeps those same sections. Hence its kernel is $\mathcal I|_{B\prime}$. By the base-change clause of the ideal correspondence this cuts out $C\times_BB\prime$. The argument of Steps 1--2 on $B\prime$ applies: $j\prime$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, because every scheme test is a scheme test for $j$. Thus this closed subspace is exactly its schematic closure. For an open restriction the identical calculation works on the full subsite of charts mapping into that open: the ring map and its kernel have exactly the same sections there. This proves commutation with open restriction directly.

proof.text: Taking the open restriction $O\to B$ in Step 3 gives $C\times_BO=O$: the restricted kernel is the kernel of the identity of $\mathcal O_O$, hence zero. Equivalently the square with $q:O\to C$ and $j:O\to B$ is cartesian. Consequently $q$ is an open immersion, and is quasi-compact: after any scheme test $T\to C$ its pullback is the pullback of the quasi-compact open immersion $j$ along $T\to C\to B$. Both assertions follow directly from the scheme-test definitions.

proof.text: Apply the same direct-image and kernel theorems to the quasi-compact open immersion $q$ to obtain a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K=\ker(\mathcal O_C\to q_*\mathcal O_O)$. The closed subspace $D=V(\mathcal K)\hookrightarrow C$ contains the factorization of $O$, by the zero-map criterion. Its composite with $c$ is a closed subspace of $B$: on scheme tests, successive quotients $A\twoheadrightarrow A/I\twoheadrightarrow (A/I)/J$ are a quotient of $A$. Minimality from Step 2 gives $C\subseteq D$, while by construction $D\subseteq C$. Thus $D=C$ and the ideal correspondence gives $\mathcal K=0$. This is the required injection $\mathcal O_C\to q_*\mathcal O_O$.

proof.text: If the image of $O$ were not dense in $C$, its closure would have a nonempty open complement $W$. Choose a nonempty affine etale scheme chart $T\to C$ lying over $W$, using an atlas and an affine open containing a point above $W$. Then $T\times_CO$ is empty. Evaluating the injection of Step 5 at $T$ gives an injection $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\to\Gamma(\varnothing,\mathcal O)=0$. This forces $1=0$, so $T$ is empty, a contradiction. Here the direct-image section formula is precisely compatible sections over $T\times_CO$. Hence the image is topologically dense.

source.place: Tags 082X (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image), 082Z (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), specialized to the quasi-compact open immersion; Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals).

proof.text: Finally let $V\subseteq B$ be an open subspace for which $O\times_BV\hookrightarrow V$ is closed. By Step 3, $C\times_BV$ is the smallest closed subspace through which this inclusion factors. The given closed subspace $O\times_BV$ itself is such a factor, so $C\times_BV\subseteq O\times_BV$; the defining factorization gives the reverse inclusion. They are equal as closed subspaces of $V$.
